newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks come off record to end shade firmer.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks come off record to end shade firmer.

text.p: Swiss shares ended just a shade above the previous close on Thursday after retreating from record territory in early trading.
Dealers said profit-taking after an enthusiastic start marred sentiment. Derivatives-related selling also pressured the market.
The blue-chip SMI index ended up 3.2 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3,913.8, off an all-time high of 3,937.5 points.
The all-share SPI added 2.46 points to 2,498.06.
One dealer said he expected the SMI to move in a range between 3,900 and 3,930 points on Friday if "there is no pressure from Wall Street".
Roche certificates, the most actively traded securities, added 30 francs to 10,160 in rumour-driven trading.
Investment Trust Pharma Vision had no comment on rumours swirling in Stockholm that a big Roche shareholder had swapped out its shares for those in Sweden's Astra.
Astra denied rumours that Roche management was in Stockholm to meet Astra.
Swiss dealers said it was improbable that Roche would plan to take over Astra. Roche is often mentioned as a possible suitor when speculation focuses on a large pharmaceutical group.
Ciba and Sandoz firmed around 0.4 percent each.
Shares in inspections group Surveillance jumped nearly two percent to 3,145. Dealers said the stocks surged after a major bank recommended the shares.
Banks were generally lower. CS Holding slumped 1.1 percent to 135 francs. UBS bearer shares and SBC slid 0.4 percent each to 1,207 francs and 253.75 francs, respectively.
Insurers generally firmed. Baloise shot up 3.3 percent to 2,960 francs.
